headline: Jets place Brad Lambert on waivers
take:
Daily Faceoff reports the Jets have placed Brad Lambert on waivers, noting he has one assist through 11 games this season and could be used more in the AHL.

Our numbers back the move. Lambert has played just over nine minutes a game so far this season, and in that short time the Jets have been outplayed with him on the ice at five-on-five. Their share of expected goals (a measure of chance quality) sits at 21 percent in his minutes, and the team's share is about 27 percentage points better with him off the ice. He has also produced less than his chances warranted, with no goals against 0.4 expected. Last season he had three goals in 25 games, so there's no strong NHL track record to lean on. Winnipeg is 4-8-3, and its 44 percent share of expected goals as a team points to a club losing the chance battle more often than not, so minutes in the bottom six matter. The Jets' bigger problem is that they have scored about ten fewer goals than their chances suggest. Lambert's waiver placement won't fix that, but it clears a spot for someone more productive.
